body.title: problem: Cannot apply repo template with only an empty commit on main
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Unknown, I can't try it for some reason (please explain)

> Didn't bother since I found the bug in the code. See bellow.

### About your usage of Forgejo

I've Forgejo running on k3s in my homelab. I mainly use it so a sandboxed/containerized claude-code can work on my issues and I can review the generated code.

### Problem description

## Summary

I like to initialize all my repos with an empty commit to main (`git commit --allow-empty -m "Initial commit"`). Forgejo cannot apply a template with just an empty commit on `main` when creating a new repo.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a template repo (select `Make repository a template` under `Advanced Settings` before creating).
2. Add an empty commit (`git clone <template-repo> && cd <template-repo> && git commit --allow-empty -m "Initial commit" && git push`).
3. Apply the template and its content when creating a new repo (select `<template-repo>` under `Use a template` → `Template` and check `Git content (Default branch)` bellow before clicking `Create repository`.

## Expected result

New repo gets created and is initialized with an empty commit on main.

## Actual result

Internal server error (500) and an unadopted repository.

## Cause

[services/repository/init.go#L43](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/commit/76d7bb7f692e0efc1f21a5748d992a68426cfb1a/services/repository/init.go#L43)

```diff
-	cmd := git.NewCommand(ctx, "commit", "--message=Initial commit").
+	cmd := git.NewCommand(ctx, "commit", "--allow- empty", "--message=Initial commit").
```

To avoid any unadopted repositories, I would suggest adding cleanup to [services/repository/template.go](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/commit/76d7bb7f692e0efc1f21a5748d992a68426cfb1a/services/repository/template.go#L128) (`util.RemoveAll(generateRepo.RepoPath())`).

### Potential workarounds

At step 2 of [Steps to reproduce](#steps-to-reproduce) add an empty git keep file:

```sh
git clone <template-repo> && cd <template-repo> && touch .gitkeep && git add -A && git commit --allow-empty -m "Initial commit" && git push
```

### Forgejo Version

15.0.9

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

I deploy Forgejo from `oci://code.forgejo.org/forgejo-helm/forgejo` on my k3s homelab. I'm running Version `15.0.9`. I use the SQLite database.

### Solutions

*Accepted solutions to address this problem will go here*

body.title: enh: Display action status indicators on PR Commits lists somewhere consistent
body.body:
### Context

With !14158 merged, two of Forgejo's four commit message toggles (that I'm aware of) now make use of [`details`/`summary`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details), enabling slightly better semantics, and retaining usefulness when Javascript isn't available. These changes were possible in part due to the relatively simple layout in each location, where the commit's Actions status indicator happened to not interfere with the layout of the commit message, or could be coerced not to. Unfortunately, this was not the case for the commits lists on PRs or branches.

On the PR commits list (e.g. https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14508/commits), the status indicator currently displays at the end of a commit message summary, just after the message toggle button if there is one. As discussed at https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14158#issuecomment-23102353, this layout leads to a few issues:
- the status indicator's position relative to the message toggle makes using `details`/`summary` for the message toggle rather difficult.
- each indicator is on a different visual "column", which feels off somehow (per @0ko's [observation](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14158#issuecomment-23312497)).

@0ko and I discussed this a little, and concluded that additional feedback is needed to redesign this part of this component.

### Enhancement description

Here are some ideas @0ko and I came up with. For reference, consider the following screenshots of the **current layout** from `/user2/multiline-commit-messages/pulls/1/commits` on the current debug server:

![The "Commits" list on a pull request. This list shows five commits, with various metadata. Some have multiline commits, as denoted by the toggle buttons that follow the message summary. Others have an Actions run status marker. Some have both of these at once. The status indicators trace a zig-zag pattern down the list.](/attachments/b976a433-f3cf-4745-8bd7-33b89852dc64)

**Status between message and hash (closer to hash)**:

![The same page as before, only the commit status now display separately from the commit message. Instead, the status markers, if any, display before the commit hash, near the rightmost side of the list item. Statuses now trace a satisfying visual "column" down the list, and no other list elements are offset.](/attachments/200e7597-b496-4130-bbe0-eafcdcf17b52)

**Status between username and message**:

![The same page as before, only the status markers display before the message summary. Statuses now trace a satisfying visual "column" down the list, and no other list elements are offset.](/attachments/64b25028-74e8-4645-9809-d4122f70db20)

Each of these options gives commit statuses their own distinct visual "column", and simplifies the layout enough to allow us to enhance these message toggles like their counterparts. I'm partial to the option that puts statuses before the commit hash, but I'd like feedback on this or other options to consider before I try a PR.

### Details and notes

You can try the layout yourself on a local debug server using `make build frontend && make test-e2e-debugserver`.

Note that this issue refers only to the PR "Commits" tab, not the PR "Conversation" view or the "Commits" list of a repo or branch.

body.title: bug: SSH public keys are not synchronized when an external account is linked via the account-linking page
body.body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

Yes, I've linked the repository below

### Description

Ran in to this on a new install so had an agent investigate it and it wrote the following:

When a user signs in through an OAuth2/OIDC source, SSH public keys advertised
by the identity provider are synchronized into Forgejo
(`updateSSHPubIfNeed` → `SynchronizePublicKeys`). However, when the same
IdP identity is attached to an *existing* local account through the
**account-linking page** (`/user/link_account` → "Sign in to link
`<provider>` to your account"), the SSH key synchronization is **never run**.

Consequence: because OAuth2 sources only synchronize SSH keys at sign-in
time (there is no cron/periodic sync for OAuth2 sources, unlike LDAP
sources), a user who reaches their account via the linking page gets **no
SSH keys at all** until they log out and perform another full OAuth2
sign-in. This is easy to hit whenever the `external_login_user` row is
gone but the local account survives — e.g.:

- an admin deletes the Forgejo account that carried the external login
  (the `external_login_user` row is cascade-deleted with it) and the person
  then re-links their IdP identity to a different local account, or
- account-linking is triggered for any other reason (renamed IdP identity,
  `ACCOUNT_LINKING` prompting, etc.).

Notably, the avatar **is** synchronized in this path (`updateAvatarIfNeed`
is called), so profile-data sync on linking is clearly intended; the SSH
key sync — the same class of provider-sourced profile data — is missing.

## Forgejo Version

16.0.5 (verified). The `forgejo` branch HEAD still has the same code
(`linkAccount()` in `routers/web/auth/linkaccount.go` does not call the sync).

Database: PostgreSQL (bug is DB-independent).
Auth source: OAuth2 / OpenID Connect (Kanidm as provider — not
provider-specific; any OIDC IdP exposing an SSH-key claim is affected).

## Reproduction

Setup:

- OAuth2 auth source (provider `openidConnect`, e.g. Kanidm/Keycloak/Authentik)
  with "Public SSH key attribute" configured and the IdP returning the keys
  (verified: the claim arrives in `gothUser.RawData` as a string array, and
  the normal sign-in path syncs it).
- A local user `alice` who signs in with password (no external login attached).
- An IdP identity that has at least one SSH public key registered.

Steps:

1. Have the IdP identity sign in via OAuth2 **for the first time**, letting
   Forgejo auto-create user `alice2` (or otherwise obtain an external login
   attached to some Forgejo account). `handleOAuth2SignIn` runs; keys sync.
2. As admin, delete Forgejo user `alice2`. The `external_login_user` row for
   the IdP identity is cascade-deleted.
3. Sign in as local user `alice` with password, then **log out**.
4. Sign in via OAuth2 with the same IdP identity. Forgejo finds no matching
   external login and shows the account-linking page; choose "Sign in" and
   authenticate as `alice` to link.
5. Visit `/user/settings/keys` — **no SSH key is present**.
6. Log out and sign in via OAuth2 again. This time the external login matches
   and the callback goes straight through `handleOAuth2SignIn`.
7. `/user/settings/keys` — the key is now present.

Observed in the instance logs (times from one real occurrence):

```
T+0s    GET  /user/oauth2/<source>/callback?...   303 -> /user/link_account
T+8s    POST /user/link_account_signin            303   (linking, sync MISSING)
        GET  /user/settings/keys                  key absent
T+27s   GET  /user/oauth2/<source>/callback?...   303 -> / (direct sign-in)
        public_key row created exactly now (created_unix in DB)
        GET  /user/settings/keys                  key present
```

The `public_key` row is created only at step 6's callback, confirming step 4
performed no synchronization.

## Expected behavior

Linking an external account should perform the same post-authentication
profile synchronization as a regular OAuth2 sign-in — at minimum the SSH
public keys, ideally the same set as the sign-in path (full name, group
flags), since the OAuth2 flow has just proven control of the identity.

## Actual behavior

`linkAccount()` only syncs the avatar and creates the external-login row:

```go
// routers/web/auth/linkaccount.go (v16.0.5, forgejo branch HEAD: same)
func linkAccount(ctx *context.Context, u *user_model.User, gothUser goth.User, remember bool) {
	updateAvatarIfNeed(ctx, gothUser.AvatarURL, u)
	...
	if !hasTwoFactor {
		if err := externalaccount.LinkAccountToUser(ctx, u, gothUser); err != nil { ... }
		handleSignIn(ctx, u, remember)
		return
	}
	...
}
```

`updateSSHPubIfNeed` is only reachable from `handleOAuth2SignIn`
(`routers/web/auth/oauth.go`), i.e.:

```
$ grep -rn "updateSSHPubIfNeed" routers/web/auth/
oauth.go: handleOAuth2SignIn -> updateSSHPubIfNeed   (only call site)
```

The `/user/link_account_signup` path (register-via-link) has the same gap
(ends in `handleSignIn` after `syncGroupsToTeams`, no SSH sync), while the
auto-registration path inside `SignInOAuthCallback` falls through to
`handleOAuth2SignIn` and therefore *does* sync — making the two manual
linking paths the odd ones out.

## Suggested fix

Upstream Gitea fixed exactly this in **gitea#34978**
("Refactor OpenIDConnect to support SSH/FullName sync", merged 2025-07-10,
closes gitea#26585 "Import SSH keys via OIDC"): the sync logic was extracted
into `oauth2SignInSync()` (`routers/web/auth/oauth_signin_sync.go` — avatar,
full name, admin/restricted group flags, SSH public keys) and it is invoked
from **both** the sign-in path and the link-account path
(`oauth2LinkAccount`).

A minimal Forgejo port would call `updateSSHPubIfNeed` for the configured
source after `LinkAccountToUser` in `linkAccount()` (and in
`LinkAccountPostRegister`), e.g. looking the source up via
`auth.GetActiveOAuth2SourceByName(ctx, gothUser.Provider)` as
`LinkAccountPostRegister` already does. Note the Gitea code cannot be
cherry-picked as-is (post-hard-fork divergence), but the change is small.

## Additional notes

- Related gap (same paths): group→team and admin/restricted-claim sync is
  also skipped when linking; Gitea's `oauth2SignInSync` covers those too.
  Out of scope for this report but worth considering in the same port.
- Server error vs. best-effort: Gitea's port logs sync failures
  (`log.Error`) rather than failing the sign-in; Forgejo may want the same
  semantics.

### Forgejo Version

_No response_

### How are you running Forgejo?

NixOS service

### Logs

_No response_

_No response_
